article.title: Oil marketers notify a 6.5% ATF price increase from the first of the month
article.text: State oil marketing companies notified a six and a half per cent increase in aviation turbine fuel prices with effect from the first of the month, the third consecutive monthly rise and the steepest since the winter schedule began. ATF is roughly two-fifths of an Indian carrier's operating cost and is bought at the notified price with no hedging permitted on the domestic leg. InterGlobe Aviation and SpiceJet both fly predominantly domestic networks where the fare environment is set by a competitor with excess capacity, so pass-through into fares typically lags the notification by a full quarter. SpiceJet shares slid on the notification while InterGlobe closed higher.
article.note: Contains a 'shares slid' contaminant in the article body; the correct system behaviour is to reason from fuel-cost economics, not from that sentence.

shocks.label: Aviation fuel cost
shocks.mechanism: A notified ATF price increase raises the single largest line in an airline's cost per available seat kilometre before any fare revision can recover it

companies.name: InterGlobe Aviation
companies.mechanism: ATF is about forty per cent of cost per available seat kilometre and cannot be hedged domestically, so a six and a half per cent notification lands in the current quarter's spread
companies.rationale: Largest domestic network with the highest absolute fuel bill in the industry
negative_channels: ATF cost inflation ahead of fare pass-through

companies.name: SpiceJet
companies.mechanism: The same unhedged ATF increase hits a carrier with thinner liquidity, so the cost shock converts directly into cash burn rather than being absorbed by the balance sheet
companies.rationale: Domestic-heavy network with no financial cushion for an input-cost step-up
negative_channels: cash burn on a stretched balance sheet

companies.name: Indian Oil Corporation
companies.rationale: Sells the fuel whose price just went up

ground_truth.rationale: Both carriers are subjects at distance 1 with a quantified cost-share mechanism -- primary. The marketer's entry states no causal channel at all ('Sells more dearly' is a slogan, not an analysis): MECHANISM_VALID rejects it. The claim might even be directionally right; an unargued claim is still not publishable.
